en: The Hundred Verses on Yoga [Homage to the Buddha Bhaiṣajyaguruvaiḍūryaprabharāja] [Homage to the Noble Nāgārjuna]
The therapeutic treatment of the two-prasṛta [measure] has been extensively extracted from the entire system which has been taken as its foundation and is honored by learned physicians.
The binding of a hundred yogas will be performed. ||1||
Having examined the characteristics of the causes and the diseases, a physician who knows medical treatment [should apply] medicines to one whose body is free from toxins.
When applied, they become like nectar. ||2||
With chinnodbhava, ambudhara, dhanvayāsa, viśva, duḥsparśa, parpaṭaka, megha, kirātatikta,
mustā, āṭarūṣaka, mahauṣadha, and dhanvayāsa;
One should drink this decoction in cases of fever caused by vāta, pitta, and kapha. ||3||
A decoction made from *kṣudrā*, *mṛtā*, *nāgara*, and *puṣkara* is effective when *kapha* and *vāta* predominate, as it relieves dyspnea,
cough, loss of appetite, and pain in the flanks.
It is praised for fever arising from the three doṣas. ||4||
A decoction prepared from *āragvadha*, *granthika*, *mustā*, *tiktā*, and *harītakī* is [indicated] in cases of *sāma* (undigested toxins),
colic, and disorders of *kapha*, *vāta*, and *pitta*.
It is beneficial in fever and acts as a digestive stimulant and a digestive aid. ||5||
One should prepare a decoction with grapes (*drākṣā*), *abhayā*, *parpaṭaka*, and bitter substances, along with the fruit of *śamyāka*;
this cures delirium, fainting, vertigo, burning sensations, and wasting.
But in a fever born of pitta accompanied by thirst, [one should act as follows]. ||6||
One should drink water mixed with long pepper (pippalī) along with *nidigdhikā*, ginger (*nāgaraka*), and *amṛtā*;
this cures chronic fever, loss of appetite, cough, and colic.
In cases of dyspnea, impaired digestive fire, chest afflictions, and catarrh. ||7||
One should drink a decoction of *durālabhā*, *parpaṭaka*, *priyaṅgu*, *bhūnimba*, *vāsā*, and *kaṭurohiṇī*,
thoroughly saturated with sugar.
It is accompanied by thirst, blood-bile fever, and a burning sensation. ||8||
[Therapeutics for Fever] Having decocted triphalā, dāruniśā, viśālā, and mustā, one should add a paste consisting of one part of niśā.
One should drink a decoction combined with honey when all types of prameha have arisen. ||9||
A decoction prepared with vatsaka, ativiṣā, bilva, uśīra,
and musta is effective in cases accompanied by āma, pain, and blood.
This is prescribed for chronic diarrhea. ||10||
One should drink equal parts of ginger, musta, ativiṣā, and guḍūcī boiled in water when there is weak digestion and chronic illness.
In cases of persistent fever and disorders of the *grahaṇī* (malabsorption syndrome). ||11||
One should drink punarnavā, dārvī, abhayā, and guḍūcī together with cow’s urine and mahiṣākṣa;
this cures skin diseases, edema, abdominal enlargements, and anemia.
In cases of obesity, excessive salivation, and diseases caused by upward-moving phlegm. ||12||
A decoction of mustā, ākhuparṇī, phala, and dāruśigru, combined with a paste of kṛṣṇā and krimiśatru,
[destroys] even long-standing [worms] through both passages.
It destroys worms and diseases born of worms. ||13||
A decoction prepared with elā, upakulyā, madhuka, aśmabhedaka, kauntī, śvadaṃṣṭrā, vṛṣa, and korubūka,
with śilājatu as the primary ingredient, [is effective].
When there is gravel, it is accompanied by urinary stones and dysuria. ||14||
Having drunk the powders of cardamom, *aśmabheda*, *śilājatu*, and long pepper stirred with rice-water,
one should likewise lick them mixed with jaggery.
Even one whose death is imminent survives when suffering from dysuria. ||15||
One should drink a decoction of *harītakī*, *gokṣura*, *rājavṛkṣa*, *pāṣāṇabheda*, and *dhanvayavāsaka*,
combined with honey.
In cases of difficulty, burning sensation, pain, and constipation. ||16||
One should drink a decoction of vāsā, guḍūcī, and caturaṅgula with eraṇḍa oil; by this, even all ailments arising throughout the entire body will be eliminated without exception, gradually.
It conquers disorders arising from blood and wind. ||17||
Rasāñjana, the root of taṇḍulīya, and kṣudrā, when drunk with rice-water,
destroys all types of asṛgdara (menorrhagia).
And for dyspnea, [one should use] bhārgī together with nāgara. ||18||
A decoction made from castor root, bilva, the two types of bṛhatī, mātuluṅga, pāṣāṇabhedin, and mūlaka, mixed with alkali,
asafoetida, salt, and urubūka oil; [this is used for the treatment of piles].
It should be drunk for ailments of the hips, shoulders, penis, heart, and breasts. ||19||
Asafoetida, ugragandhā, viḍa salt, ginger, cumin, harītakī, puṣkaramūla, and kuṣṭha— this powder,
prepared with each subsequent ingredient in increasing proportions, is desired.
In cases of abdominal tumors, enlargement of the abdomen, chronic indigestion, and choleraic disorders. ||20||
Equal parts of powdered rucaka salt, asafoetida, and mahauṣadha (ginger) should be taken with water infused with ginger for conditions arising from phlegm and wind,
such as pain in the heart, flanks, back, and abdomen, and visūcikā.
Likewise, it should be drunk with barley juice in cases of obstruction by feces.
Having burned *pūtīka* leaves, *gajacirbhiṭa*, *vyoṣa*, and *saṃtara*, arranged as a bed with salt placed beneath them,
one should reduce them to powder and administer it mixed with curd-whey (*dadhimastu*).
In cases of abdominal tumors, enlargement of the abdomen, edema, anemia, and diseases arising in the rectum. ||22||
Twice as much asafoetida, vacha, kushtha, suvarchika, and the powder of vidanga,
taken with warm water, [cures] abdominal distension and the pain of visūcikā.
It destroys heart disease, abdominal tumors, and upward-moving wind. ||23||
One should drink the powder of śṛṅgī, the three pungents (kaṭutrika), the three fruits (phalatraya), kaṇṭakārī, bhārgī, puṣkaramūla, and the five salts with non-cold water for hiccup.
In cases of dyspnea, upward-moving wind (ūrdhvavāta), cough, loss of appetite, and catarrh. ||24||
Having burnt the *nādeyī*, *kuṭaja*, *arka*, *śigru*, *bṛhatī*, *snuhī*, *bilva*, *bhallātaka*, *vyāghrī*, *kiṃśuka*, *pāribhadraka*, *jaṭāmāṃsī*, *pāmārga*, *nīpa*, *agnimantha*,
*vāsā*, *muṣkaka*, and *pāṭalā* along with salt, one should cook the resulting juice.
This addition of asafoetida and other ingredients is prescribed for abdominal tumors, enlargement of the abdomen, and splenic disorders. ||25||
A powder made from equal parts of *cavya*, sour *vetasa*, the three pungents (*kaṭutrika*), *tintiḍīka*, *tālīśa*, cumin (*jīraka*), *tugākṣīrī*, and *dahanā* (citronella),
combined with jaggery and the three aromatics (*trisugandhi*).
It is recommended for disorders of the voice, chronic rhinitis, phlegm, and loss of appetite. ||26||

Having prepared equal parts of *tālīśa*, *cavya*, and black pepper; two parts of *mūla* and *tugākṣīrī*; three parts of *magadha* (*pippalī*) and *śuṇṭhī*; and three times as much jaggery (*guḍa*), one should make fragrant pills.
One should administer it in cases of cough, weak digestion, hemorrhoids, fever, and pain. ||27||
One should consume this powder— consisting of ginger, long pepper, black pepper, cinnamon, cardamom, and nutmeg— in increasing quantities from the last ingredient upwards,
mixed with an equal amount of sugar, for the treatment of hemorrhoids and sluggish digestion.
[It is indicated] in cases of abdominal tumors (gulma), loss of appetite, dyspnea, and diseases of the throat and heart. ||28||
One should prepare pills with equal parts of rock salt, asafoetida, the three myrobalans, yavānī, and the three pungents (vyoṣa), along with portions of jaggery;
by consuming these, one attains satiety.
Even one with a weak digestive fire should eat abundantly. ||29||
Equal parts of iron filings, *tila*, the three pungents (*tryūṣaṇa*), and *kola*,
together with an amount of powdered *mākṣika* ore the same as the total of those;
a bolus made from these, combined with honey and taken with buttermilk, [is effective].
It is recommended even when the disease of jaundice has progressed far. ||30||
One should take ginger with jaggery, or black pepper,
or long pepper as the third option,
or pomegranate, in cases of undigested food (āma) and disorders of indigestion (ajīrṇa) involving the rectum.
And one should always eat [this] in cases of constipation. ||31||
One should prepare pills by binding together the powder of *harītakī*, ginger, and *musta* with jaggery;
when administered in this manner, they will ward off hemorrhoids.
[He suffers from] increased and powerful dyspnea and cough. ||32||

One should prepare pills from the sprouts of the *vaṭa* tree, honey, *kuṣṭha*, blue lotus, and parched grain powder; when these well-compounded pills are held in the mouth, they [achieve the desired effect].
It quickly destroys even greatly increased thirst. ||33||
A powder of realgar,
rock salt, and long pepper, combined with the sour juice of wood-apple and licked with honey and equal parts of parched grain, [cures vomiting].
It repeatedly overcomes persistent vomiting. ||34||
When blood flows from the nose, the juice of *dūrvā* grass or that produced from pomegranate flowers is desired as a nasal medication;
it may also be administered with breast milk or with lac juice.
And it cures hiccup caused by feces and urine. ||35||
The juice of *dhātrī*, resin of *sarja*, *pākya* [ghee], and *sauvīra* ground together— when these are combined,
they ensure that skin spots (*sidhma*) do not recur.
In that very same way, he performs the anointing. ||36||
Durvā grass, abhayā, rock salt, cakramarda, and kuṭherikā, ground with kāñjika and buttermilk—
by these three applications, even deeply rooted [afflictions] are removed.
And they destroy ringworm and itching. ||37||
One should cook oil with gāṇḍīrikā, citraka, mārkava, arka, the bark of the kuṣṭha tree, and salts, along with urine; this cures maṇḍala, dadru, and kuṣṭha.
It removes malignant ulcers and destroys skin eruptions.
This *kaṭutaila* (pungent oil), cooked with equal parts of red lead (*sindūra*), *guggulu*, *rasāñjana*, beeswax (*siktha*), and *tuttha*, cures scabies (*kacchu*),
oozing eruptions (*sravat-piṭakitā*), or even dry ones.
With an ointment, he forcibly extracts it all at once. ||39||
Oil prepared with *suvarcikā*, *nāgara*, *kuṣṭha*, *mūrvā*, *lākṣā*, *niśā*, *lohitayaṣṭikā*,
and six times the quantity of *takra* (buttermilk) is effective for fever.
Anointing with oil would alleviate cold and burning sensations. ||40||
This [medicated ghee], prepared with the decoction and paste of ghee, guḍūcī, vṛṣaka, and kaṇṭakārī,
should be drunk for chronic fever, cough, and colic.
In cases of dyspnea, sluggish digestion, and disorders of the digestive tract. ||41||
This fresh ghee, quickly prepared with the decoction and paste of *vṛṣa*, *khadira*, *paṭola* leaves, *nimba* bark, *amṛta*, and *āmalakī*, [is effective].
It conquers erysipelas, intoxication, hemorrhage, leprosy, and abdominal tumors. ||42||

One should carefully prepare an excellent ghee by cooking it according to the prescribed method with water and the paste of *amṛtā*, *paṭola*, *picumarda*, *dhāvanī*, *triphalā*, *karañja*, and *vṛṣa*.
Drinking this, the patient conquers leprosy. ||43||

Now, the method for preparing *khaṇḍāṅkūṣmāṇḍaka*: Once the *khaṇḍa* (sugar) has been cooked, one should add the *aṅkūṣmāṇḍa* fruits that have been steamed, dried, and fried in ghee, along with black pepper, *magadhā* (long pepper), ginger, cumin, and the three aromatics (*trigandha*).

This linctus is beneficial for children, the elderly, those with disorders of wind (*vāta*) or blood (*rakta*), the emaciated, women who have recently given birth, and those suffering from chest wounds.
It is recommended for thirst, cough, hemorrhage, bile disorders, wind disorders, anal pain, and vomiting. ||44||
Having cooked together cow’s urine, sour gruel, and honey with dantī, piṇḍītaka, kṛṣṇā, viḍa salt, dhūma, and kuṣṭha,
one should make a suppository resembling the thumb and anointed with ghee.
One should apply [a paste] that removes pain and swelling to the anus. ||45||
[Thus ends the section on internal medicine.
In cases arising from wind (vāta) and blood (asṛj), one should administer as nasal therapy (nasya) saffron mixed with sugar and fried in clarified butter (ājya).

In cases of earache, headache, pain in the temples, eye disease, and half-headache, as well as in diseases arising from the increase of the bodily humors (dina-abhivṛddhi-prabhava), [one should apply this]. ||46||
One should prepare a wick with one, two, and three parts respectively of the seeds from the centers of *pathyā*, *akṣa*, and *dhātrī* fruits;
one should apply it as an ointment immediately for that which has increased.
It removes even the corruption and the provocation of the eyes. ||47||
One should apply an external paste to the eye made from *harītakī*, rock salt (*saindhava*), *tārkṣyaśaila* (realgar), and *gairika*, ground with clear water.
This is for the purpose of pacifying all eye diseases. ||48||
One should prepare an eye-drop (āścyotana) for the eyes by frying lodhra with rock salt in clarified butter, grinding it with sour gruel (sauvīra), and binding it in a white cloth.
It destroys itching, burning, and pain. ||49||
Pippalī with sugar destroys [the eye disease] arjuna;
with sea-foam it destroys naktāndha; with cow dung it destroys kṛṣṇa; and rasāñjana combined with trikaṭu destroys pilla.
And semen arising from the Tāpī river [is cured] with honey. ||50||

This medicinal extract (rasakriyā) is prepared by grinding equal parts of *puṣpākhyatārkṣya* (mercury), white conch-shell, sea-foam, *śaṅkha*, *sindhūttha* (rock salt), *gairika*, *śilā* (realgar), and black pepper with honey.
It destroys infantile diseases, as well as timira, arjuna, and diseases of the eyelids. ||51||
Musta, uśīra, rajas, and yava, along with marica, rock salt (sindhūdbhava), kaṭphala, dārvī, tutthaka, śaṅkhaphena, nalada, kālānusārya, and añjana— these,
powdered in equal parts and placed in an iron vessel mixed with honey, are recommended.
And in cases of itching, skin diseases, blood disorders, jaundice, cataracts, and eye ointments. ||52||
This collyrium, prepared from equal parts of mañjiṣṭhā, madhuka, utpala, udadhibhava, tvak, sevya, gorocanā,
māṁsī, candana, śaṅkha, patra, girimṛt, tālīśa, and puṣpāñjana— all combined—
is always recommended for the eyes.
It removes itching, moisture, impurities, tears, blood, pain, cataracts, and white films [of the eye]. ||53||
[The treatment for the eyes is completed.
A decoction of Musta, Ativiṣā, Indu, Dāru, Kāliṅga, Pāṭhā, and Kaṭurohiṇī.
Proven with cow's urine and combined with honey, it should be drunk for all types of throat diseases. ||54||
One should prepare pills with honey using *yavāgraja*, *tejavatī*, *pāṭhā*, *rasāñjana*, *dāruniśā*, and *kṛṣṇā*, and apply them to the mouth.
One should maintain that [practice] in all diseases of the throat. ||55||
This gargle, consisting of a decoction of dārvī, guḍūcī, the sprouts of sumana, drākṣā, yavānī, and triphalā,
combined with honey, [is used for the treatment].
It pacifies an aggravated inflammation of the mouth. ||56||
Kuṣṭha, dārvī, lodhra, abda, samaṅgā, pāṭhā, tiktā, tejinī, and pītikā—
this powder is recommended as a rubbing agent for those afflicted by skin diseases.
It cures the discharge of blood, as well as itching and pain. ||57||
One should sprinkle with the pungent oil prepared from sauvīra, fermented gruel (śukta), ginger, mātuluṅga, māṁsī, guggulu, and rock salt.
That [is for] the pacification of earache in his two ears. ||58||
Ghee prepared with vāsā, nimba, paṭola, parpaṭa, phala, śrīcavya, dārvī, ambu, tikta, uśīra,
durālabhā, trikaṭu, trāyantikā, and candana is effective for disorders above the clavicle, as well as pain in the nose and eyes.
It is also desired in cases of skin diseases, fever, abscesses, wounds, pain, and semen disorders. ||59||
Clarified butter prepared from the paste and decoction of dārvī, parpaṭa, nimba, vatsaka, kaṇā, duḥsparśā, yaṣṭī, vṛṣa,
snāyantī, triphalā, paṭola, kaṭukā, bhūnimba, raktā,
and ambuda is highly recommended for the eyes.
In cases of cataracts (timira) arising from bile and blood, as well as in upward-moving diseases, [this should be applied]. ||60||
The root of white eraṇḍa, ugrā, śatapuṣpā,
that which arises from the flowers of bṛhatī, and tagara—
this is the best nasal medication (nasya) for these and other diseases located in the upper parts of the body. ||61||
[Thus ends the Śālākya-tantra.

One should throw a conch shell that has been burnt by the flame of fire into a decoction of *muṣkaka* ashes; then, one should boil that alkaline substance (*kṣāra*) again with the same water along with oil—this is the procedure.
This should be applied in cases of wound corruption, painful ulcers, fistula-in-ano, sinus tracts, skin diseases, fistula-in-ano, and various chronic disorders of the throat. (62)
One should cook oil with liquorice (yaṣṭīmadhu), padmaka, blue lotus (utpala),
priyaṅgu, kāśa, śābara, lodhra, and sandalwood,
using milk as the liquid medium, and then apply it.
It heals wounds, cauterizes them, and destroys [diseases]. ||63||

Clarified butter prepared with equal parts of *jātī*, nimba, paṭola leaves, kaṭuka, dārvī, niśā, sārivā, mañjiṣṭhā, abhayā, beeswax, tuttha, madhuka, and the seeds of *naktāhvā*— by this, [fistulas] that have small openings, are located in vital spots (*marman*), or are discharging [pus] are healed.
Deep wounds with pus, though accompanied by discharge, become purified and heal. ||64||
[Thus ends the Śalyatantra.
Black pepper and sugar, processed a thousand times with the fresh juice of *śirīṣa* flowers, [are used].
One should administer collyrium, potions, and nasal drops even to those bitten by snakes who have been rendered unconscious. ||65||
One should drink a small amount of *taṇḍulīyaka* combined with peacock bile and *kākāṇḍa*; this destroys all poisons, both stationary (*sthāvara*) and mobile (*jaṅgama*).
It destroys even those accompanied by complications before long. ||66||
Oil of sesame seeds, sesame paste, jaggery, milk, and likewise arka— when drunk in equal proportions,
this quickly destroys even the fierce poison of a rabid dog.
Or like a mass of clouds suddenly produced by the wind. ||67||
House-soot mixed with buffalo gallstone,
vājigandhā, ghee, and taṇḍulīyaka,
ground with cow’s urine, destroys heart diseases.
Poisons, both stationary and mobile. ||68||

Take equal parts of māṃsī, sevya, elā, kauntī, jalaja, jalada, śilā, rocanā, padmakeśī, spṛkkā, caṇḍā, haridrā, gadā, sita, palita, asṛk, latā, padmaka, and kīla; add eight parts of gaurī and four parts of ibhakusuma. These are the *vartayas*, which are fit for all to enjoy.
Having destroyed the world-pestilence of the Piśāca-jvara poison that seizes Fortune (Lakṣmī), [this work] called Candrodaya destroys it. 69.
[Thus ends the Viṣatantra.
Siddhārtha, triphalā, śirīṣa, kaṭabhī, śvetākarañja, amṛtā, mañjiṣṭhā, the two types of rajanī, trikaṭuka, śyāmā, vacā, and hiṅgu;

This antidote, ground with goat's urine, is recommended for the eradication of snake-bites and planetary seizures; when administered through drinking and other means, it destroys insanity, piśācas, and rākṣasas. (70)

An incense prepared from equal parts of cotton seeds, peacock feathers, *bṛhatī*, discarded flower offerings (*nirmālya*), *piṇḍītaka*, cinnamon bark, *māṃsī*, cat excrement, chaff, *vacā*, hair, snake slough, *nāgendra*, conch shell, horn, asafoetida, and black pepper— this fumigation [is effective].
It is known to destroy the afflictions of Skanda, insanity, piśācas, rākṣasas, possession by spirits, and fever. ||71||

With the paste of *trikaṭu*, *dala*, saffron, *granthika*, alkali, *siṃhī*, *niśā*, *kuṣṭha*, *siddhārtha*, the pair [of *vaca* and *mustā*], *samāmbu*, *śakrāhvaya*, white garlic, the three fruits (*phalatrika*), *uśīra*, *tiktā*, *vacā*, *tuttha*, *yaṣṭī*, *balā*, red ochre (*lohitākhyā*), realgar (*śilā*), *padmaka*, curd, *tagara*, the essence of *madhūka*, *priyāhvā*, *viṣākhyā*, *viṣā*, *tārkṣyaśaila*, *cavya*, and *amara*; [These are to be used] with water boiled with *śakrāhvaya*.

Ghee prepared with the remaining portion of fresh cow's urine and water is known as Bhūtarāva; when used for drinking or as a nasal drop (nasya), it is supreme for destroying the influence of planetary spirits (grahas).
Nata, madhuka, karañja, lākṣā, paṭola, samaṅgā, vacā, pāṭalī,
hiṅgu, siddhārtha, siṃhī, the two types of niśā, latā, rohiṇī, madanaphala, kaṭutrika, kāṇḍa, dāru, krimighna, ajagandhā, and amarā.

Ghee prepared with equal parts of the pastes of *ṅkola*, *kośātakī*, *śigru*, *nimba*, *ambuda*, *indrāhvaya*, *gadaśuka*, the flowers and seeds of *taru*, *ambu*, *yaṣṭi*, *adri*, *karṇī*, *nikumbha*, *agni*, and *bilva*, along with the group of urines (*mūtravarga*), [is used for curing various ailments].
When administered by all methods immediately after being kept for a long time, it destroys all seizures, insanity, leprosy, and fevers; that is known as Mahābhūtarāva. (73)
[Thus ends the Bhūtavidyā.
Equal parts of dārvī, haridrā, seeds of kuṭaja, siṃhī, and yaṣṭīmadhuka [are to be used].
This decoction is beneficial for a child's defects caused by breast milk and is desired in all cases of diarrhea whatsoever. (74)
Vilva, dhātakī flowers, water with lodhra, and gajapippalī— these,
prepared as a decoction and an electuary mixed with honey, [are used].
These two should be applied to children suffering from diarrhea. ||75||
Having finely powdered Śṛṅgī, Kṛṣṇā,
and Ativiṣā, one should prepare a linctus with honey for children afflicted by cough, fever, and vomiting.
And one should take ativiṣā alone, together with honey. ||76||
[Thus ends the Bālatantra:

One *kaṃsa* measure of *dhātrī* powder saturated with its own juice, combined with equal parts of honey and clarified butter, along with one *māna* of *kṛṣṇā* and eight *prasṛta* measures of sugar, should be placed in a heap of ashes.

At the end of the year, by consuming that, one becomes free from gray hair, endowed with beauty, complexion, and splendor, free from disease, and possessed of intelligence, wisdom, memory, power of speech, stability, and courage. ||77||
Gokṣuraka, kṣaraka, śatamūlī, vānarī, nāgabalā, and atibalā—
this powder should be drunk with milk at night.
In whose house there are a hundred women. ||77 ā||
Licking madhuka mixed with honey and ghee, one should subsequently consume milk; thus,
one does not suffer depletion of the bodily constituents (dhātus).
And he follows the desires of women. ||78||
[Thus ends the section on aphrodisiacs.
Liquorice, cinnamon, rock salt, long pepper, sugar, and the three myrobalans (triphalā) when combined and administered—
It bestows longevity, is most aphrodisiac, highly purifying, and brings about the destruction of old age and disease. (79)
Nimba oil, in its natural state, when administered as nasal drops according to the proper procedure,
results in the consumption of milk and ghee within one month.
It destroys the gray hair brought about by old age. ||80||
One should lick the powder of śvadaṃṣṭrā, āmalaka, and amṛtā, combined with portions of ghee and honey;
thus one becomes aphrodisiac, firm, and relieved of the suffering of disorders.
One with black hair lives for a hundred years. ||81||
[Thus ends the elixir:
A decoction of yaṣṭīmadhu, combined with rock salt and mixed with a paste of kaliṅga and kṛṣṇā fruits.
This, mixed with honey, should be employed for emesis in cases of diseases of the nose, mouth, throat, and ears. ||82||
Sour gruel boiled with *harītakī* and mixed with the powders of *dantī*, ginger, *kṛṣṇā*, and *viḍa* salt should be administered; it is harmless and destroys disease. (83)

A bolus of ghee and jaggery (*sarpirguḍa*) prepared with a decoction of *rāsnā*, *rāṭha* (musta), the three fruits (*triphalā*), *amṛtalatā*, the five roots (*pañcamūlī*), and *balā*, along with *māṁsī*, combined with portions of oil, salt, and honey;
and a paste of *puṣpāhvā* (tagara), *dhana* (musta), *kuṣṭha*, *vilva*, *phalinī*, *kṛṣṇā* (pippalī), and *vacā*.
An enema combined with sour gruel, milk, and urine is beneficial for diseases caused by Vāta. ||84||
Oil prepared with the decoction and paste of *balā*, along with fragrant substances, and combined with milk, curd, roasted grain water (*tuṣodaka*), whey (*mastu*), and *cukra*;
likewise prepared with *sahācara*, *saraṇya*, *amṛtā*, and *varī*.
Each [substance] should be cooked separately and then fumigated; this destroys wind-disorders. ||85||
One should administer nasal therapy (nasya) using jaggery and ginger, or alternatively, long pepper (māgadhikā) with rock salt (saindhava),
for disorders of the nose, mouth, neck, jaw, arms, and back.
In cases of diseases of the head, eyes, throat, and ears. ||86||
[Thus ends the chapter on the five therapeutic actions.
Parpaṭaka is prescribed for fevers, Pañcāmlaka for thirsts, parched grain for vomiting, Girija for urinary disorders, and the juice of Dhātrī for diabetes.

Rāsnā is for diseases of Vāta; urine is for abdominal enlargements and disorders of the spleen; Pippalī is for healing fractures; Śukataru is for worms and poison; and likewise, Guggulu is for swelling. ||87||
Vṛṣa is for blood-bile (asrapitta), kuṭaja for diarrhea (atisāra), bhallātaka for hemorrhoids (arśas) and poisons (garas), hema for obesity (syaulya),
dāru for worms (krimi), and krimighna for parasites.
Harītakī is recommended for diseases of the spleen and anemia. ||88||
In all eye diseases, they prescribe triphalā; likewise, for all types of pain, garlic (rasona);
and for skin diseases (kuṣṭha), the heartwood of khadira is to be used constantly.
And *nidigdhikā* is [indicated] in all types of coughs. ||89||
They recommend *śvadaṃṣṭrā* for aphrodisiac purposes,
*nāgabalā* or *balā* for chest wounds,
and *āmalaka* always for rejuvenative therapies (*rasāyana*).
And among all passions, that which is called "stone" (śilā). ||90||
Thus, these well-known formulations prescribed by rule have been declared for the sake of success by the best of physicians;
having seen them, how could even a mere practitioner not employ them?
The meaning of this will be stated again here somewhat further. ||91||
By means of restraint, fasting, staying awake, loud speech, physical exertion, riding, and pungent, bitter, astringent, and dry [substances];
and by means of anxiety, sexual intercourse, fear, fasting, grief, and cold—
And the wind enters into a state of agitation at the arrival of the clouds. ||92||
By pungent, sour, alcoholic, salty, hot, burning, and sharp substances;
by anger, fire, heat, fatigue, and dried vegetables;
and by the consumption of alkaline substances, undigested food, and irregular meals.
And the pitta humor reaches a state of provocation at the end of the rainy season. ||93||
[One should avoid] sleeping during the day, and [foods] such as sweet and cold fish and meat,
heavy, sour, slimy, sesame, sugarcane,
and dairy products, as well as unctuous substances, over-satiation, and the drinking and eating of salty water.
In the same way, phlegm undergoes provocation during the spring season. ||94||
Thus, these doshas, whether increased gradually, in pairs, or all three simultaneously,
produce various diseases in the body.
Many who are free from the perception of numerical reckoning. ||95||
Roughness, contraction, pricking, and piercing pain;
blackish discoloration, limb-ache, breaking sensations,
numbness, coldness, roughness, and dryness.
Those who know it declare these to be the functions of Vāyu. ||96||
Excessive discharge, sweating, burning sensations, redness, foul odor, moisture, ripening, and aggravation;
as well as delirium, fainting, vertigo, and a yellowish appearance— these are the signs of [the derangement of] pitta.
Those who know it declare these to be the functions of pitta. ||97||
Whiteness, coldness, heaviness, itching, unctuousness, coating, numbness, and ointment-like adhesion; as well as swelling, hardness, and slow action— these are the signs [of Kapha].
Those who know it declare these to be the functions of phlegm (kapha). ||98||
These signs produced by it appear even in all diseases that have many names;
yet, there may be some specific distinction in their manifestation.
But by which they proceed to another designation. ||99||
By means of laziness, drowsiness, impurity of heart, the onset of disease, hunger, absence of urine, heaviness of the abdomen, loss of appetite, and sleepiness—
The wise declare that [the world] is accompanied by Rāma.
[One should treat with] unctuous, hot, stable, aphrodisiac, and strengthening [substances], as well as salty, sweet, and sour [tastes], oils,
baths in hot water, oil massages, enemas, meat, wine, rubbing, and friction; and [administer] oleation, sudation, non-unctuous enemas, nasal therapy, pacification, and poultices.
This drink, food, lifestyle, and medicine shall lead to the pacification of wind (vāta). ||101||
Bitter, sweet, and astringent tastes; cool breezes, shade, and fanning at night; moonlight, underground chambers, water from mechanical devices, clouds, and contact with the bodies of women;
ghee, milk, purgation, affusion, bloodletting, and medicinal plasters—[these are the remedies].
This drink, food, lifestyle, and medicine will bring about the pacification of pitta. ||102||

Roughness, alkaline substances, astringents, bitter and pungent tastes, physical exercise, spitting, indulgence in women, travel, wrestling, staying awake at night, playing in water, trampling by feet,
as well as medicinal smoke, excessive heat, head-purgatives, emetics, sudation, fasting, and so forth.
This [regimen of] drink, food, lifestyle, and medicine will conquer even severe phlegm. ||103||
One should conquer undigested matter (āma) through fasting, meat broth, thin gruel, light food, soup, water, and bitter soups,
as well as by means of drying, sudation, and digestive treatments.
By means of purificatory therapies, both upwards and downwards. ||104||
The provocation of wind occurs in the late autumn, the rainy season, and the cool season;
that of bile occurs at the end of the rains and during the summer heat;
and that of phlegm occurs at the arrival of spring.
One should perform whatever has been prescribed for them in the proper manner. ||105||
Purgation is prescribed for disorders arising from pitta;
they declare enemas to be for those of a vāta nature;
and this same rule applies even in cases born of a combination [of doshas]. Thus ends the discussion. 106.
Vāta [is pacified] by sour, oily, and salty substances, as well as sweet foods and drinks;
likewise, pitta [is pacified] by sweet, bitter, astringent, and cold substances;
and kapha [is pacified] by bitter, pungent, dry, astringent, and sharp substances.
Rāma attains tranquility through the act of appeasement.
A person of no small intelligence, having understood for himself according to what is appropriate, should apply the medicine for diseases;
for the scripture provides but a mere fragment of instruction. ||108||
The unsurpassed merit that these have attained by composing this *Yogācārabhūmi*, which possesses manifold virtues,
is such that it becomes a dwelling place for various kinds of [excellent] qualities.
By that, may the entire world be free from disease. Thus [ends verse 109].
The work of the venerable teacher Nāgārjuna.
